title: I Tried Coding a Neural Network to Identify Doodles
beats: Wants computer to recognise doodles; recounts past failed neural net experiments (walkers, cars)
Sequence: digits, fashion, doodles, colour images
Invents a purple spiky poisonous fruit with two features
Plot size of spots vs spike length; decision boundary separates safe from poisonous
Two inputs, two outputs; one output per class for future problems
Weights as importance; output is weighted sum; code Classify and Visualize
Slides weights by hand; boundary only rotates; adds bias to shift it
Throws away hand-written code for Layer and NeuralNetwork classes
Extra layer does nothing without nonlinearity
Neuron fires if stimulus enough; activation function; bias as threshold
Abrupt output changes; swaps for sigmoid
Computer needs a measure; counting correct fails; squared-difference cost
Trial-and-error is possible on tiny network but will not scale
Minimise one-input function; slope by tiny h nudge
Gradient descent as sliding down into valley; learning rate too small, too big, local minimum
Two weights make a cost landscape in 3D; same idea in more dimensions
Learn code nudges every weight; fruit learns but slow
Faster way costs calculus; quick refresher
Derivative of x^2-3x+4 by expanding with h, shrinks to 2x-3
Cannot set h zero; careful limit notation; derivative graphed against slope
Three-node network with two weights and chain rule
Three partial derivatives multiplied, each derived in turn
Notes tidied to node values; backprop code, layer by layer
Names backpropagation; compares to one pass per weight
MNIST digits: 784 inputs, 784-dim space imagined as 3-D
Hidden layer, 95%, then 97% after lowering learn rate
Own handwriting breaks it; centring dependence; augmentation and noise help
Probes weaknesses by editing a one; overfit
Quick Draw doodles, 87%, drawing live; helicopter weakness
Colour images only 53%; promises convolutional upgrade

theory: The network is built so that each piece appears only after the previous design visibly fails. Hand-tuned sliders create the need for each component, brute-force nudging creates the need for calculus, and the derivative is introduced as the exact version of the nudge the learner already ran.
velocity: Scene builder: slider-controlled boundary scenes where failure is felt before the fix appears
Orchestrator: model 'component as repair' so the next concept is gated on a visible failure
Ghost hands: show nudge-and-measure before derivative notation
Learner model: calculus refresher beat only if the learner shows weak slope intuition
Evals: check every new term follows a failure within a minute
quote: we don't want to be put in maths jail
